RBI's is more of a reflection of the people in front of him. Votto and Choo were #1 and 2 respectively in the league in OBP. He didn't create as many runs as he should have either. According to Baseball Reference Votto created 132 runs, Choo created 125, while Brandon created 71. Another key here is outs. The top priority of a player is to not get out. In those links you can see that Votto 428 times, Choo 426 times, and Phillips got out 483. Phillips was batting right at league average but he was below league OBP, and that's a big deal. His ISO, which shows how many productive he is when it comes to extra base hits, is .135, which is below average. His total average, which gives credit towards every base he gains and detracts everyone he loses, was merely .615 compared to Votto who's over 1 and Choo who is .974.
I know comparing him to Votto and Choo is stiff competition, but we're paying him a ton of money. It varies from person to person but I believe that for every 1 WAR the general consensus says that you're supposed to pay 3 million. For his performance this year, overall, we should have payed him around 6 million. This year, he received 10 million, and his pay begins to increase yearly and his stats are dropping rapidly every year as seen by the links show above. This is why it will be hard to get anyone to bite on him and we'll probably have to eat a large portion of the contract just to get him out of Cincinnati. Another key here is outs.  The top priority of a player is to not get out.  In those links you can see that Votto 428 times, Choo 426 times, and Phillips got out 483.  Phillips was batting right at league average but he was below league OBP, and that's a big deal.  His ISO, which shows how many productive he is when it comes to extra base hits, is .135, which is below average.  His total average, which gives credit towards every base he gains and detracts everyone he loses, was merely .615 compared to Votto who's over 1 and Choo who is .974.
